text:
Anya: Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the GA follow-on micro release (targeting next Tue). Can we land a cut that prioritizes customer-impacting bug fixes and one small enhancement?
Sam: +1. What are the must-fix bugs today?
Leo: p99 reconnect on streaming sessions (investigated, looks like backoff logic regression) — hitting 2 large customers. Severity: high.
Maria: Also seeing incorrect token attribution in billing logs for routed fallback requests. Leads to billing noise for a handful of accounts. Severity: medium-high.
Tim: Embedding cache per-tenant (enhancement) would drop embedding cost ~20% for sample workload; low risk but needs schema change and migration.
Anya: My proposal: release = bug-fix-focused (p99 reconnect + billing logs) + 1 enhancement (tenant embedding cache) if we can keep migration safe. Cutoff: freeze on Friday EOD for code + migration runbook.
Sam: That feels reasonable. What's the ETA on reconnect fix?
Leo: I have a patch in PR, unit + integration tests pass, needs canary on dedicated. If we can perf canary tomorrow morning it should be safe.
Maria: Billing logs fix is a small change in tracing layer, I can push a patch today. Can validate against staging replay data.
Tim: For embedding cache: migration is optional (feature flag). I can implement as opt-in behind FF; if migration looks risky we can postpone. Effort ~2 dev-days.
Anya: OK — final plan: 1) prioritize reconnect fix + billing logs in release. 2) Try to include embedding cache behind FF as opt-in, but do not block release if migration not ready. 3) Set rollback criteria and canary checks.
Sam: Rollback criteria suggestion: if canary p99 increases >5% or error-rate on streaming endpoints >0.5% over baseline -> rollback. Agree?
Leo: Agreed. I'll run canary against a 5% traffic slice and dashboard the p99 and error-rate.
Maria: I'll run staging replay for billing fix and attach before/after logs to the release ticket.
Tim: I'll land the FF and basic cache code behind feature flag, docs + migration in follow-up if we don't ship.
Anya: Good. Who owns the release ticket and validations?
Sam: I'll own release coordination + rollback runbook. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROD-1872
ops-bot: Deploy window scheduled: 2026-03-24 02:00 UTC -> 02:40 UTC (canary then full). Reminder: run preflight checks 30m prior.
Anya: Preflight checklist (short): 1) smoke tests passing; 2) canary metrics present; 3) migration runbook + backup in place; 4) customer communications draft ready.
Leo: I'll post canary perf dashboard link once ready.
Maria: Draft customer note for impacted accounts ready, tagging CS for approval.
Sam: I'll schedule a 15m post-deploy check point at +30m to confirm metrics.
Anya: Great — final action items: Leo (canary + PR), Maria (billing fix + logs), Tim (FF for cache opt-in), Sam (release owner + runbook). Cutoff Fri EOD for merges. If anything blocks, ping here. :thumbsup:
Leo: copying steps to PR.
Maria: staging replay started.
Tim: FF pushed to branch, I'll open PR today.
Sam: Running checklist.
Anya: Thanks team — let's aim for a clean, low-risk micro release.
__notes: This thread summarizes a short post-launch planning sync focused on bugs vs enhancement tradeoffs and release coordination. Messages are in chronological order and reflect realistic Slack brevity (mentions, bot reminder).
